summary_ja: 金融庁長官が内部評価方式を承認する際に審査するABCPプログラムの運営に関する基準と内部評価制度の設計及び運用に関する基準の内容を定める。
summary_en: Sets out the standards on the operation of ABCP programs and on the design and operation of the internal assessment system that the Commissioner examines when approving use of the internal assessment approach.
paragraphs: In intending to grant the approval under Article 239 for the use of the internal assessment approach, the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency shall examine whether the operation of the ABCP program for which the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach plans to use the internal assessment approach conforms to the "standards on the operation of ABCP programs" provided in the next paragraph, and whether the operation of the internal assessment system by that Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal ratings-based approach conforms to the "standards on the design and operation of the internal assessment system" provided in paragraph (3) (referred to as the "standards for approval" in the next Article).

The "standards on the operation of ABCP programs" in the preceding paragraph means the following. (i) A rating by an eligible credit rating agency has been assigned to the ABCP, and that rating conforms to the standards on the eligibility of ratings in securitization transactions provided in Article 238, paragraph (2). (ii) In selecting the eligible credit rating agencies that assign ratings to the ABCP, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company does not select only rating agencies with relatively lenient rating methodologies, and, where a selected eligible credit rating agency changes its rating methodology (including stress factors), considers the necessity of changing the standards of the internal assessment. (iii) Guidelines on the acceptance of assets in the ABCP program have been established, and those guidelines set out an outline of the structure of the purchase transactions of the original assets. (iv) Credit analysis of the risk characteristics of the transferor of the original assets in the securitization transaction is performed. (v) Standards on the eligibility of the original assets to be purchased have been established, including the following and other matters: (a) Prohibition of the purchase of receivables that are overdue for a long period and receivables in default. (b) Limits on concentration of credit to individual obligors or regions. (c) An upper limit on the maturity of receivables that may be purchased. (vi) In order to prevent potential deterioration in the credit quality of the underlying assets of the ABCP, the ABCP program incorporates, for each pool of underlying assets of the securitization exposures, measures concerning the purchase of assets such as asset purchase stoppage measures. (vii) The ABCP program sets out collection procedures that take into account the performance capability and credit risk of the servicer. (viii) The ABCP program has taken measures to reduce the risks that may arise with respect to the transferor of the original assets in the securitization transaction and the servicer, in order to maximize the collection of principal and interest on the underlying assets.

The "standards on the design and operation of the internal assessment system" in paragraph (1) means the following. (i) The internal assessment of the credit risk of the securitization exposure to the ABCP program conforms to the assessment criteria that eligible credit rating agencies use for the original assets purchased in that ABCP program, and is equivalent to investment grade or higher as of the date of the initial assessment. (ii) The internal assessment is incorporated into the management information and capital allocation systems and other internal risk management processes of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, and is in line with the minimum requirements for the internal ratings-based approach prescribed in Section 4 of the preceding Chapter. (iii) The internal assessment procedures identify the degree of risk, and the correspondence between each internal assessment and the ratings of eligible credit rating agencies is clearly defined. (iv) The internal assessment process (including the stress factors for determining the level of credit enhancement) is more conservative than the assessment criteria published by the major eligible credit rating agencies (limited to those that rate ABCP backed by the same type of assets as the original assets purchased in the ABCP program subject to assessment in the internal assessment process). (v) Where ratings by two or more eligible credit rating agencies have been assigned to the ABCP and the levels of credit enhancement required to obtain equivalent ratings differ, the stress factors of the eligible credit rating agency requiring the more conservative level of credit enhancement are used. (vi) The rating methodologies of eligible credit rating agencies are published for the assets or exposures subject to assessment; provided, however, that this does not apply where, for a new or special transaction not covered by the rating methodology of the eligible credit rating agency that rates the ABCP, the approval of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency has been obtained for using the internal assessment method for the ABCP based on that transaction. (vii) Internal or external auditors, an eligible credit rating agency, or the credit assessment department or risk management department within the Ultimate Designated Parent Company periodically audit the internal assessment process and its effectiveness. (viii) The persons who conduct the audit in the preceding item are independent of the client-facing and ABCP sales departments within the Ultimate Designated Parent Company. (ix) The track record of operations under the internal assessment approach is continuously recorded in order to evaluate it, and, where the performance of exposures consistently deviates from the corresponding internal assessments, adjustments are made as necessary. (x) In estimating the losses of the original asset pool being considered for purchase in the ABCP program, all factors relating to credit risk, dilution risk and other possible risks are taken into account.
